sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: email: unique lookup for auth/identity resolution; manager_id: team views and approval routing by manager; employment_status: filtering active employees for leave eligibility

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: entitlement lookup by leave type (annual/sick/emergency); is_active: filtering active policies for balance accrual

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: employee self-service history and balance reconciliation; status: manager approval queues and query filtering; leave_type_id: filtering by leave type; start_date, end_date: time-off calendar range queries and overlap detection

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: balance lookup for an employee; policy_id: entitlement source join; fiscal_year: per-year balance isolation; employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year: unique balance row per employee/policy/year (enforced uniqueness)

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: audit trail lookup for a specific record; performed_at: chronological audit reporting; action: filtering by action type (APPROVE/REJECT)

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: inbox lookup for a user; status: filtering unread/pending notifications; related_entity_type, related_entity_id: linking notifications to leave requests
data_notes: Six conceptual tables: employees, leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances, audit_logs, notifications. leave_requests.leave_type_id references leave_policies.id (policy carries the leave_type enum: annual/sick/emergency). leave_balances enforces uniqueness on (employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year). Audit (GP-002) and RBAC (GP-005) are satisfied via audit_logs and employees.manager_id. Two binding open questions recorded for day-count and rounding semantics (BR-001 anti-pattern avoided).

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted when computing used_days and remaining_days (e.g. inclusive vs exclusive of end_date, half-day support, weekend/holiday exclusion, rounding direction)?
open_questions.impact: This quantity is consumed by balance deduction on approval, balance display, and overlap detection. If each call site computes it independently, balances will drift and approvals may over/under-deduct. Must be a single shared computation.
candidate_options: Inclusive day count (end_date - start_date + 1), no half-days, no weekend/holiday exclusion
Exclusive day count (end_date - start_date), no half-days
Business-day count excluding weekends and company holidays
Support half-day granularity (0.5 increments) with a half_day flag on the request

open_questions.question: What is the rounding direction and precision for remaining_days when entitlement is fractional (accrual_rate present) or when used_days is fractional?
open_questions.impact: remaining_days = total_entitlement - used_days must be computed consistently across balance display, approval checks, and accrual jobs; inconsistent rounding can cause a request to appear approvable in one place and rejected in another.
candidate_options: Store full precision and round only at display

transaction_contract: Leave approval/rejection is a multi-step atomic write: update leave_requests.status + approved_by/approved_at, increment leave_balances.used_days (and recompute remaining_days), and insert an audit_logs row. Repository methods that must join a caller's transaction take an optional pg PoolClient/executor parameter (defaulting to the shared pool when omitted). The service owns the unit of work: acquire a client from the pool, BEGIN, pass the client to each repository call (leave request status update, balance update, audit insert), then COMMIT or ROLLBACK on error. Balance deduction and audit write must never commit independently of the status change.
